{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.5 (Commerce One / Corio)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Agreement — verified findings only

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook. The commercial architecture is broadly favourable to us on the points that most often cause problems: there is no exclusivity, no non-compete, no MFN, no minimum purchase or volume commitment, no non-solicit, no liquidated damages or early-termination fee, and the Vendor IP indemnity in Section 8 is uncapped by operation of Section 9 — better than our fallback.

Our concerns are concentrated in seven deviations and two gaps:

- **One walk-away item.** Section 13.5 flips ownership of Corio-created Developments to Commerce One wherever Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis. That is an assignment of our own IP to the Vendor and cannot stand.
- **The liability cap is effectively illusory.** Section 9 limits recovery to amounts paid "for the transaction which the liability relates to", a per-transaction slice rather than 12 months' fees, and there are no carve-outs for confidentiality, gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
- **No exit and no landing.** There is no transition assistance or data-export obligation on expiry or termination, and no Vendor insurance anywhere in the document — in a hosting arrangement where Commerce One personnel operate in our environment, both are needed.
- Remaining deviations are narrower and targeted at the fallback: arbitration in place of California courts (Section 14.3), consent-based assignment with no reasonableness standard (Section 14.1), no affiliate extension of the Section 2 licences, a 60-day software warranty cut off at 31 December 1999 (Section 7.3), and audit notice/cost-shifting thresholds in Section 4.4.

**Verification flag:** the termination-for-convenience finding (§ 11) did **not** pass verification and is marked *needs review*. We should not raise or rely on that position until the underlying text and the proposed Section 11.3 numbering are re-checked against the document.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 8 INDEMNIFICATION | Vendor IP indemnity with duty to defend and full remedy ladder; carved out of the Section 9 cap, so uncapped — above fallback. No redline. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 13 SHARED RESOURCES | Carve-out in 13.5 transfers Corio-created Developments to Commerce One where it provides ongoing support; no licence-back for embedded Vendor IP, no no-joint-ownership statement, no data-ownership clause. Walk-away territory. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 9 LIMITATION OF LIABILITY | Cap is per-transaction rather than 12 months' fees; no carve-outs for confidentiality, gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Mutuality and the indemnity exception are already acceptable. |
| 4 | High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | Exhibit D — Sales and Marketing Cooperation | Licences are non-exclusive; Exhibit D cooperation is expressly non-binding. No sourcing commitment on us. |
| 5 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties | Compliant | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION | No early-termination fee, minimum fee or acceleration; audit cost reimbursement is cost recovery, not a penal sum. |
| 6 | High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § 13 SHARED RESOURCES | No competing-product or post-term restraint; § 13.6 confirms independent development is permitted. |
| 7 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Needs review (verification failed)** | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION | Finding records a five-year term with exits limited to breach and insolvency and proposes a new § 11.3. Verification did not pass — re-confirm before use. |
| 8 | Medium | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 14 MISCELLANEOUS | Mutual clause with successor carve-out, but consent is at absolute discretion and there is no notice mechanic for successor assignments. No change-of-control termination right. |
| 9 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | § 14 MISCELLANEOUS | California law is acceptable at fallback; § 14.3 mandatory AAA arbitration displaces the California courts, failing the forum element. |
| 10 | Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 2 GRANT OF RIGHTS | Grants are perpetual, irrevocable and transferable on a successor event, but do not extend to Corio's affiliates and no affiliate concept exists. |
| 11 | Medium | MFN | Compliant | § 4 FEES | Fees fixed by Exhibit B; no matching, best-offer or comparable-customer obligation on us. |
| 12 | Medium | MINCOMMIT | Compliant | § 4 FEES | Unlimited users, one-time licence fee, activity-based variable fees; the 40-user "minimum limitation" is a qualifying condition, not a spend commitment. |
| 13 | Medium | NOSOLICIT | Compliant | § 14 MISCELLANEOUS | No non-solicit, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant binding either party. |
| 14 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION | One-year renewals with a 30-day either-party non-renewal window; no renewal uplift right. Absence of a Vendor reminder is a minor point only. |
| 15 | Medium | TRANSITION — Exit assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION | Only exit mechanic is the mutual confidential-information return sentence in 11.3; no transition assistance and no data export obligation. Escrow releases source code only on Release Conditions. |
| 16 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 7 WARRANTIES AND DISCLAIMER | Real conformance warranty with correction/refund remedies, but the software period is 60 days from the Effective Date and capped at 31 December 1999 — below the 90-day fallback. |
| 17 | Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | § 4 FEES | Once-yearly, independent accountant, Vendor-borne cost; but notice is only "reasonable" and cost-shifting triggers at a >5% shortfall rather than >10%. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 14 MISCELLANEOUS | No coverage obligation anywhere; Commerce One personnel operate in our hosted environment and it runs the MarketSite.net Service. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

1. **Section 13.5 ownership flip (IP, critical).** Ownership of Developments created solely by Corio must not pass to Commerce One merely because Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis. We require deletion of that carve-out, a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back for any Commerce One IP embedded in Developments, confirmation that the parties will not jointly own IP, and a short sentence preserving our rights in Corio and Customer data. Commerce One's retention of its own Software (§ 2.8) and pre-existing materials is unaffected.

2. **Section 9 cap (LOL-CAP, critical) — walk-away in substance if unmoved.** A cap measured only by amounts paid for the single related transaction is effectively illusory. We require a true 12-month fees cap and carve-outs for breach of confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct. We are not pressing the USD 1,000,000 floor, "paid or payable", or the additional preferred carve-outs; the mutual consequential-damages exclusion stays.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** on the seven deviations and two gaps, in this order of priority: § 13.5 ownership; § 9 cap and carve-outs; new transition/data-export clause in § 11; insurance clause in § 14 (E&O USD 1,000,000; cyber/privacy USD 2,000,000); § 14.3 exclusive California court venue with conforming amendment to the § 12.2 cross-reference; § 7.3 warranty period to 90 days with the 31 December 1999 outside date deleted; § 2 affiliate extension on written notice; § 14.1 reasonableness standard plus successor-assignment notice; § 4.4 fifteen days' notice and a >10% cost-shifting trigger.
2. **Re-verify the termination-for-convenience position** before it is tabled. The finding failed verification, and the proposed clause would need to be numbered and drafted consistently with the existing § 11 scheme and the defined term "CUSTOMER(S)" (§ 1.6, meaning Corio's sublicensees).
3. **Confirm negotiating authority** on the two walk-away items and on our floor for the liability cap.
4. **Leave the compliant items alone.** Indemnification, exclusivity, non-compete, liquidated damages, MFN, minimum commitments, non-solicit and renewal all meet or exceed our positions; several benefit us and should not be reopened.
5. **Record the noted-but-not-flagged points** (indemnity scope limited to the Software; no renewal reminder; no injunctive-relief carve-out; no affiliate/competitor limbs in assignment) in the deal file in case they become tradeable later."}
